hints: Focus on the direction of Group 2 trends as you go down, since barium is above radium so radium is further down.
Remember that reactivity with water increases down Group 2, and solubility of hydroxides also increases down the group.
Recall the opposite trend for sulfates, solubility decreases down the group, then check which combination includes all three true statements.
walkthrough:
**Locate barium and radium in Group 2**

Barium is above radium, so radium is lower down Group 2. All trends must be applied downwards from Ba to Ra.

Trend rule: reactivity increases down Group 2.

**Check reactivity with water - statement 2**

Down the group the outer electrons are further from the nucleus and more easily lost, so reaction gets more vigorous.

$$\text{M(s) + 2H}_2\text{O(l)} \rightarrow \text{M(OH)}_2\text{(aq) + H}_2\text{(g)}$$ 
So radium reacts more vigorously than barium. Statement 2 is correct.

**Check hydroxide solubility - statement 1**

Group 2 hydroxides become more soluble down the group. $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ is almost insoluble, $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ is quite soluble.

So $\text{Ra(OH)}_2$ should be even more soluble than $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$. Statement 1 is correct.

**Check sulfate solubility - statement 3**

Group 2 sulfates show the opposite trend, they become less soluble down the group. $\text{BaSO}_4$ is already almost insoluble.

So $\text{RaSO}_4$ should be even less soluble, meaning $\text{BaSO}_4$ is more soluble than $\text{RaSO}_4$. Statement 3 is correct.

**Combine the conclusions**

Statements 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. That matches the 1, 2 and 3 combination.

options.A: Correct. All three statements follow the Group 2 down-group trends. Hydroxide solubility increases so Ba(OH)2 < Ra(OH)2, reactivity increases so Ba < Ra, and sulfate solubility decreases so BaSO4 > RaSO4.
options.B: Incorrect. This option includes only statements 1 and 2. While those are true, it wrongly leaves out statement 3. Sulfates do get less soluble down the group, so barium sulfate is correctly more soluble than radium sulfate.
options.C: Incorrect. This option includes only statements 2 and 3. It wrongly leaves out statement 1. Students sometimes confuse hydroxide and sulfate trends, but hydroxides become more soluble down the group, so statement 1 is true.
options.D: Incorrect. This option includes only statement 1. It misses the reactivity trend and the sulfate trend. Both statement 2 (increasing reactivity down the group) and statement 3 (decreasing sulfate solubility) are also true.
